key_terms.ارْكَبُوهَا: Ride on them; use as saddle coverings or riding equipment
key_terms.السِّبَاع: Predatory animals (lions, wolves, tigers, etc.); those with claws that hunt prey
key_terms.تُصَلُّونَ فِيهِ: While praying in it; wearing it during salat

ai.seo_question: Can Muslims use predatory animal skins for riding or wearing during prayer according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about the permissibility of using the skins and hides of predatory animals (such as lions, wolves, and leopards). He distinguished between two uses: riding on such skins — for example as saddle coverings — is permitted, whereas wearing them as clothing during salat is forbidden. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that predatory animal skins are ritually impure (najis) and thus cannot be worn during prayer, though their use as riding equipment does not invalidate prayer.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about skins of the predatory animals, so heasws said: ‘Ride in them but do not wear anything from these while offering Salaat (Praying in them)’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the skins of beasts. He (the Imam) said, ‘You can use them when riding but you must not use them during performing Salat (prayer).”’
